## Overview

Backpressure in a streaming pipeline is the mechanism by which a slow downstream consumer signals an upstream producer to reduce its emission rate. Without backpressure, an unbounded buffer grows until the process runs out of memory.

## Common Implementations

Backpressure can be implemented through several approaches:

- **Bounded queues**: The producer is blocked once the queue reaches capacity, preventing further writes until the consumer drains items.
- **Credit-based flow control**: The consumer explicitly grants the producer permission to send N more items. The producer only transmits when it has available credits, which the consumer replenishes as it processes items.
- **Reactive-pull models**: The consumer requests items on its own schedule, rather than the producer pushing items unconditionally. This inverts the flow direction and gives the consumer direct control over the rate of consumption.

## Significance

Backpressure is essential for stable, memory-efficient operation of streaming and event-driven systems, preventing cascade failures and resource exhaustion when downstream components cannot keep pace with upstream production rates.
